_README: REVIEWED date formatting. ONE DATE FORMAT, ONE PLACE THAT WRITES IT (owner
2026-08-18: '全套系统的 date format 没有统一'). Every date a user reads is
DD/MM/YYYY and comes from fmtDate/fmtDateTime in
frontend/src/vendor/shared/format.ts (mirrored in backend/src/scm/shared/
format.ts). backend/scripts/check-date-formatting.mjs finds lines that SPELL a
date by hand; a regex cannot read intent, so this file is where a person
records the judgement. Every entry needs a `why` that would survive being read
out loud. A line not listed here FAILS the build - that is the whole point:
silence becomes a decision.
Keyed by (file, normalized line text) and NOT by line number, so a merge that
moves a line keeps its review and an EDIT to a line re-opens it.
Entries whose line is gone are reported as STALE and printed, never failed - a
gate that punishes somebody for fixing a line is a gate that stops fixes.
The four legitimate cases, so they do not have to be re-derived:
1. ISO VALUE PRODUCERS. A date input's value, an API payload, an AutoCount
field and a sort key are all YYYY-MM-DD. Storage is not display and is
outside this rule entirely.
2. A WEEKDAY or MONTH NAME used as a LABEL - a calendar header, a chart
bucket, 'Monday' beside a fmtDate. It names a period, it is not a date.
3. A RANGE compression that prints the year once ('31 Jul - 2 Aug 2026').
4. A NAMED PERSON'S NAMED DECISION on a printed or outbound document. Those
are listed with the person and the date, and changing one needs them.

reviewed.why: printedStamp — the ASSR sign-off footer, specified by Nico 2026-07-30 as 'yyyy/mm/dd hh:mm AM/PM'. A named person's named decision on a printed sheet; changing it needs him, not this pass.
Month LABELS for a chart bucket / KPI card ('August target'), not dates. The label names a period; no day is involved.
Month LABELS for a chart bucket / KPI card ('August target'), not dates. The label names a period; no day is involved.

Feeds fmtRange only — '31 Jul - 2 Aug 2026' for an event SPAN on the printed run sheet, specified from the owner's reference sheet 2026-08-12. Deliberate compression of two dates into one line; the plain fields on the same sheet use fmtDate.
A PERIOD label ('August 2026') for the POS stats window — names a month, not a day. The day-level labels in this file now come from fmtDate.

The Seampify WhatsApp payload. DEFERRED: the downstream template lives OUTSIDE this repo and expects YYYY/MM/DD, so changing it here could break a customer message. Needs whoever owns that template — flagged in the PR body.

ISO VALUE PRODUCER, not a display: en-CA renders YYYY-MM-DD, which is what the date input / API payload wants. Storage stays ISO and is outside this rule. (Separate known bug, unchanged here: en-CA reads the DEVICE clock, so a machine outside GMT+8 produces the wrong Malaysian day — todayMY() is the timezone-stable fix.)
